subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy and audit consumers?
rationale: This would add public Plugin SDK and Gateway security-policy facts, and related open proposals cover provenance, default-deny permissions, audit egress intent, and runtime Security Matrix facts.

options.title: Approve unified descriptor contract
options.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventory, Gateway protocol, and hook events, and document that declarations do not bypass host policy.

options.title: Fold into capability permissions
options.body: Keep this issue blocked behind the broader default-deny capability permission model so descriptors ship only as part of an enforceable grant subsystem.

options.title: Limit to Security Matrix
options.body: Use the audit model as the first consumer and defer a general-purpose public descriptor field until that vocabulary lands.

recommendation.title: Approve unified descriptor contract
recommendation.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics, thread them through tool definitions, plugin metadata, inventory, Gateway protocol, and hook events, and document that declarations do not bypass host policy.
